title: Wordmark width proofs
instruction: Compare each piece at both wordmark widths at actual size, so Dustin can choose one.
intro: Dustin Cathcart, our founder and editor, chooses the wordmark’s width from these proofs. Each proof shows one piece at actual size at today’s width and at the condensed width, both with ampersand B, set on one edge or one line so the wordmark is the one thing that changes. Today’s width stays in use until he chooses.
We recommend today’s width. At the same height the condensed drawing only runs narrower, and its heavy capitals sit close to the lettering of campaign signs. Its monogram also reads as 0&A.

groups.label: The marks at a glance
text: The wordmark from each of its masters, the stacked lockup and the monogram, both widths at the same height.

items.label: Both widths
items.caption: At the same height the condensed wordmark runs about a fifth narrower: 152 against 120 px from the 16 px masters, 221 against 181 from the 24 px masters, and 435 against 342 from the display masters at 48 px tall.

groups.label: Masthead on the site
text: L3 in the 1440 px site bar and L1 in the 390 px phone bar, today’s width above the condensed width on one left edge.

items.label: Both widths, stacked
items.caption: At the same height the condensed wordmark runs 40 px shorter, so the lockmark moves 40 px to the left. Use Fit to window to see each bar whole.

groups.label: Masthead in email
text: L3 at the head of a 600 px email, the two widths side by side. A sent email carries the masthead as a PNG at twice size, with the alt text “Oath & Action”.

items.label: Both widths, side by side
items.caption: The story under each masthead is invented.

groups.label: Avatar
text: The monogram, L8, on the Charcoal tile that Rule 04.7 sets as the default, in a circle and a square. A feed draws an avatar at about 32 to 48 px, where L8 at either width sets its capitals under the 14 px floor. Rule 04.7’s avatar, ampersand B alone, reads at that size and is the same at both widths, so we recommend it whichever width Dustin chooses.

items.label: Both widths, side by side
items.caption: L8 fills 62 percent of the tile’s width at both widths, so the condensed capitals stand taller, and its narrow O reads close to a zero.

groups.label: Social card
text: The 1200 by 630 link-preview card, today’s width above the condensed width on one left edge, with its specifications under them.

items.label: Both widths, stacked
items.caption: Until chapter 23 sets social cards, build one from these specifications at today’s width.

groups.label: Letterhead
text: US Letter, 8.5 by 11 inches, at true size on screen, 96 px to the inch, the two widths side by side. The print proof holds both widths, one per page, each labeled; check its scale with a ruler before you judge it on paper.

items.label: Both widths, side by side
items.caption: The address, recipient and letter are invented, and the letter is signed with Dustin’s name and title.

groups.label: Minimum sizes at both widths
text: The smallest size of each mark whose size changes with the width. Chapter 03 lists today’s width alone.

items.label: Both widths
items.caption: From the identity masters’ table. Every other mark keeps its minimum at either width.
